groups.defect: Google CalendarService stores the zod SafeParse wrapper ({success,data}) as the credential key instead of `.data`, and it parses the merged credentials instead of the refresh response. In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but the Google, zoho-bigin, zohocrm and HubSpot callers read `.data`. zoho-bigin also passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId.
groups.rationale: Several members report two of these defects together: s_1e21d54f, s_fe509f7a and s_c52b0e89 report both the SafeParse wrapper and the Response shape, and s_af2d6511, s_f54d5082 and s_afc19080 report both the Response shape and credentialId. Because of these overlaps, the three defects form one chained group.

groups.defect: In minimumTokenResponseSchema, the computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` resolve to fixed junk strings, so the schema always fails in sync mode. The literal 'refresh_token' placeholder is also injected and saved, overwriting real refresh tokens.
groups.rationale: All three report the broken computed-key schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse. Two of them also report the placeholder refresh_token issue.

groups.defect: The webhook secret is compared with a non-constant-time `!==`, and array-valued or missing headers are not handled. The parse and decrypt calls are also unguarded, so bad input returns a 500.
groups.rationale: Both report the timing-unsafe secret comparison and the array-header handling. s_751abf53 also reports the unguarded parse and decrypt calls.

groups.defect: In Office365, parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws on an invalid refresh response instead of tolerating it, and the error logging was removed.
groups.rationale: Both describe the same behaviour regression at the same lines.
